abstraction_design.rationale: The core abstractions are shaped around real variation and stretch well to an Items-like section, but the home page bypasses buildCards and a few near-duplicates (card factories, panel scaffold, MoveTable columns) would be copied rather than reused.

findings.issue: The home page builds Pokémon card objects inline, duplicating the card construction that buildCards does in lib/server/pokeapi.js; changes to card shape or sprite logic must be made twice, and this pipeline has no Pokémon records so it can't be fixed the same way buildCards can.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single card factory (shared by buildCards and the species-list path, e.g. a buildCardsFromSpecies sibling) so every list of cards is produced in one module.

findings.issue: Sprite URL pattern '/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png' is duplicated here and in pokeapi.js spriteUrl (line 146); a media-URL change needs two edits.
findings.suggestion: Export spriteUrl from the data module (or include the sprite in a shared card factory) and import it in the home loader.

findings.issue: The column set is defined three times in the component (columns array, valueFor switch, hardcoded <td> cells) plus makeRow on the server, so adding/removing a column touches four spots across two files.
findings.suggestion: Drive headers and cells from one column descriptor list (key, label, renderer) so the definition exists once per side.

findings.issue: Two mechanisms carry the same fact: the card object already has a hidden field (pokeapi.js:159) but the component reads a separate hidden prop, only passed by abilities/[name]/+page.svelte:27; other pages silently ignore the data field.
findings.suggestion: Drop the prop and read pokemon.hidden (or derive it) so the data is the single source.

findings.issue: buildCard and hiddenCard are near-duplicates that differ only in the hidden flag — exactly the boolean-flag creep that grows when card fields change.
findings.suggestion: One factory with a hidden parameter, or set hidden after construction.

findings.issue: All component styles (e.g. .pokemon-card at 210, card-grid at 201) live in a 596-line global stylesheet, so editing a component's appearance means editing a distant file and relying on an implicit class-name contract rather than Svelte's scoped styles.
findings.suggestion: Co-locate component styles in <style> blocks (PokemonCard, MoveTable) and keep only tokens/layout/shared classes in app.css.

findings.issue: The section/panel scaffold (<section class="panel" aria-labelledby> + h2 + '<count> Pokémon' intro) is hand-repeated in every page template, so a scaffold change or a new Items-like page copies it again.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small Section snippet/component (heading slot + children) and reuse it across pages.

findings.issue: Home hardcodes <title>Pokédex</title> while its loader also returns title: 'Pokédex' (+page.server.js:87) — the server-returns-title convention used by every other page is inconsistent, and the returned field is dead data.
findings.suggestion: Render {data.title} like the other pages (or stop returning it).

findings.issue: mapLimit, a generic concurrency utility, is defined in and exported from the API module, so a future generic helper either stays stranded in a data file or triggers a move-and-reimport across loaders.
findings.suggestion: Move it to a neutral #lib/util module.

findings.issue: The `type-badge type-${name}` class composition is hand-built in five templates (also MoveTable.svelte:93, moves/[name]/+page.svelte:19, types/[name]/+page.svelte:22, PokemonCard.svelte:15), an implicit convention spread across the UI.
findings.suggestion: A tiny TypeBadge component (or shared snippet) would centralize the class scheme and link building.

summary: A well-structured SvelteKit 3 app with a genuinely good data layer: server-only memoized fetching, centralized formatting rules, and presentational components with narrow interfaces, so most changes land in one predictable place. The main editability cost is the home page's parallel card/sprite pipeline that duplicates buildCards and would force any card-level fix to be made twice, once without access to the data needed. Secondary seams (MoveTable's triple-defined columns, repeated panel scaffold, global-only styles) are small but will each require copy-paste when stretched.
